items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I went over to see him. I sat down at a table and listen to him play. And he came off the bandstand while everybody was playing, and he crouched beside me at the table and we were talking.

ctx.x: Did you have a sense that he was going to be a major innovator?

Oh yeah, sure. I’ll tell you why. Because if I’d go and hear Miles, I remember the first time I heard Trane. I went to — Miles was advertised someplace on the east side. There was, it was in the 70s or something like that, there was a jazz club over there. And I went over to see him. I sat down at a table and listen to him play. And he came off the bandstand while everybody was playing, and he crouched beside me at the table and we were talking. And he was saying, “Wait ‘till you hear this tenor player.” He says…
Right. This, wow — they made some great records too.
